description: Masala Maggi Noodles are a beloved Indian comfort food, transforming instant noodles into a flavorful, spicy, and satisfying meal. This quick recipe elevates the classic Maggi with fresh vegetables and aromatic spices, creating a truly irresistible dish. Perfect for a quick snack or a light dinner, it's a taste of home in every bite.

instructions.title: Prepare Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a pan or kadai over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and green chili (if using). Saute until the onion turns translucent, about 2-3 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Tomatoes and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the finely chopped tomato. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the tomatoes soften and release their juices. Add the red chili powder and garam masala. Mix well and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Incorporate Vegetables
instructions.text: Add the peas and finely chopped capsicum to the pan. Saute for 2-3 minutes, allowing the vegetables to cook slightly but remain a bit crunchy. This adds texture and freshness to your Maggi.

instructions.title: Add Water and Taste Makers
instructions.text: Pour in the water and add both Maggi taste maker packets from the instant noodles. Stir thoroughly to combine all the ingredients and dissolve the taste maker. Bring the mixture to a rolling boil.

instructions.title: Cook the Maggi Noodles
instructions.text: Once the water is boiling, break the Maggi noodle cakes into the pan. Submerge them gently in the water. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the noodles are soft and most of the water has been absorbed, leaving a slightly saucy consistency.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the pan from heat. Garnish generously with freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve your hot and spicy Masala Maggi Noodles immediately as a comforting snack or a quick meal.

tips: For an extra rich flavor, you can add a small knob of butter or a splash of milk towards the end of cooking.
Experiment with vegetables like corn, shredded cabbage, or grated carrots to customize your Masala Maggi. A dash of lemon juice at the end brightens the flavors.
Masala Maggi is best enjoyed fresh and hot. If you prefer it less soupy, cook for an extra minute or two until the liquid is almost fully absorbed.
